origin.objective_verbatim: Describe the movement of the Moon around the Earth.
origin.source_type: Accepted lesson source record supplied in SC3R3 baseline set

outcome: I can explain why the Moon appears to change shape as it orbits Earth.

arrival: Name one useful feature and one limit of an orbit model.
What force keeps planets in orbit?
Predict why the visible lit part changes.
arrival_starter.starter: Look at new, quarter and full Moon. What might be changing?

routes.choice: Match new, quarter and full Moon cards to the model views. Choose the cause: changing view of the lit half / the Moon changing shape. In your book, label one view and finish: We see ___ because ___.
routes.aspire_text: AspireExplain the phase sequence, distinguish eclipses and name one model limit.Help with The Moon's JourneySeparate changing viewpoint from blocked sunlight; explain the tilted orbit.
routes.independent: Sequence four model positions and explain why the visible lit part changes.
routes.supported: Match new, quarter, full and quarter views with a partner.Help with The Moon's JourneyUse a fixed sunlight arrow and point to the lit half.Small supported promptsHelp with The Moon's JourneyThe Moon appears… because we see… as it orbits…

must_know_words: an object that orbits a planet
the shape of the lit part of the Moon visible from Earth
a curved path around another body
light that changes direction from a surface
method_steps: Keep the cool light fixed and use one Moon model or the prepared phase cards.
Mark the lit half and the observer position. Stop and check the light direction with the adult.
Sequence four views from the same observer, keeping phase and eclipse explanations separate.
In your book, label an observation and conclude why the visible lit part changes. Restore lighting and return equipment.
P17_staff_support: Give time to start → point to the relevant place → rephrase → offer a small prompt or word bank → reduce to a limited choice. Never straight to telling the answer.
P18: Retained existing target placeholders and opportunities in lesson Guidance.

teacher_questions.1: Why does the Moon appear to change shape?
teacher_questions.2: What force keeps planets in orbit?
teacher_questions.3: Look at new, quarter and full Moon. What might be changing?
teacher_questions.4: Which half of the Moon does sunlight illuminate?
teacher_questions.6: How does light travel from the Sun to the Moon and then to an observer?
teacher_questions.7: Is this observation an ordinary Moon phase or an eclipse, and what is the clue?
teacher_questions.8: How does the sequence of model positions explain the changing view of the lit half?
teacher_questions.9: Which phase explanation will you improve, and what evidence supports the change?
teacher_questions.10: Why are ordinary phases not caused by Earth’s shadow?
